Autoplot Methods for VAR Models

Source: R/autoplot.R
autoplot.Rd

autoplot() uses ggplot2 to draw a plots for objects created with tv_*() functions in a single command.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tv_fevd'
autoplot(object, .impulse = NULL, .response = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_irf'
autoplot(object, .impulse = NULL, .response = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_augment'
autoplot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_tidy'
autoplot(object, type = c("estimate", "statistic"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_causality'
autoplot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_predict'
autoplot(object, .n_obs = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_causality'
plot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_fevd'
plot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_irf'
plot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_predict'
plot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_augment'
plot(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tv_tidy'
plot(object, ...)

Arguments

object

An object, whose class will determine the behavior of autoplot.

.impulse

A character. The variable to be used as impulse. Defaults to NULL.

.response

A character. The variable to be used as response.

...

Other arguments passed to specific methods.

type

The column that should be plotted.

.n_obs

A double. The number of observations to be included in the plot.

Value

A ggplot2 object.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

model <- vars::VAR(EuStockMarkets)

autoplot(tv_fevd(model))

autoplot(tv_irf(model))
